name: BugHerd
summary: Visual bug tracking and website feedback. Let clients and teams point-and-click to report issues right on the page, turned into trackable tasks.
best_for: web agencies and site teams that want clients to point-and-click feedback directly on the page — and, new in 2026, want AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and others) to read, triage and action that feedback via BugHerd's MCP server, free in beta
skip_if: you don't work with external clients or website revisions (a plain issue tracker is enough), or you need deep dev-workflow tracking that belongs in Jira
honest_knock: The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly: your clients report for free as guests, but everyone on your side who works the feedback needs a seat, so a growing agency steps up tiers. It's deliberately a visual-feedback layer, not a full project-management or dev-issue tracker — most teams run it alongside Jira/Trello rather than instead of. The new MCP feature is genuinely interesting but currently beta: treat AI-agents-triaging-your-feedback as a bonus to evaluate, not the reason to buy.

pricing.notes: Standard $42/mo billed yearly or $50 month-to-month (5 members, 10 GB), Studio $67 or $80 (10 members, 25 GB), Premium $125 or $150 (25 members, 50 GB), plus a custom tier quoted as "Let's talk" — all with unlimited projects and unlimited client users; annual billing reads $500/$800/$1,500 a year ("two months free"), extra members $8 per user billed monthly or $6.60 billed annually ($80 a year each). Free trial; 60-day money-back guarantee; data export via CSV, XML and JSON on every plan. Prices in US dollars excluding applicable taxes (re-verified 13 October 2026 on bugherd.com/pricing; unchanged since our July read). MCP and auto-title generation sit in every plan, auto-tagging and similar task detection in Premium and up, all still marked beta.

friction.format: CSV (22 columns) or JSON/XML with one row per task; screenshots as links, no attachments or design files.
friction.reimport: Not testable: we found no import function.

lost: The changed title of task 2: the export has no title column; only the updated time moved
The uploaded design itself: the export only links to a screenshot

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 24 October 2026 during the trial, without a card and without inviting anyone: Daan created the account and installed the BugHerd Chrome extension, and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We left one feedback task on a website (example.com) and one on our own uploaded test design, changed the title of the second task, and exported both tasks as CSV and JSON.
findings: Before you reach the task board you must install BugHerd on a site: the setup window 'Learn to use BugHerd in 3 simple steps' could not be closed (Escape did nothing) until the extension or a script was in place.

Leaving feedback on a page opens a form with description, assignee, severity, status, due date and tags, and captures a screenshot automatically. The task then appears on the board with the screenshot, URL, browser and operating system.
An uploaded image (PDF, image or Figma are offered) becomes a design asset with the same feedback sidebar; our pin on the test design became a task labelled 'IMAGE'.

The export (CSV, XML or JSON) arrived as an email attachment within about 15 seconds. Both tasks came back with description and metadata, but not the title we had changed on task 2 (there is no title column), and not the uploaded design itself, only a screenshot link. Those screenshot links opened without logging in.
In Settings, creating tasks by email and commenting on tasks by email were both switched on by default, and archived tasks are left out of the export unless you switch them on.
The header said '7 days remaining! Upgrade now!' and no card was asked. We found no import function.
not_tested: Inviting clients and the client view
Installing via a script on our own site
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
